There's tons of stuff serious preppers keep supplies of, but here are some basics for anyone wondering how to start.

There are a lot of things that could be added to this list, just do some research online to learn more.

1-2 two weeks supply is a good start, 2-3 months is better, and if you can get set up for a year or longer, go for it.

After you have a good supply going, be sure to use some of it as it ages to rotate out the old stuff.

If the power goes out, you never know how long it'll be until it comes back (if ever)

Make sure to stock supplies for yourself & family, and your pets if possible.

Top Priorities:

  • Water (short term: bottles/jugs - long term: filtration/purification methods, rain collection)

  • Food (short term: boxed/canned goods, beans, rice, oatmeal - long term: MREs, dehydrated & freeze-dried foods, gardens)

  • Ways to make fire & cook: (matches, lighters, flints, camp stove, grill, pots/pans, cups/bowls/plates/utensils)

  • Home defense (basic: knife, machete, axe - better: bow/crossbow - best: pistol/shotgun/rifle w a few hundred rounds)

  • Shelter/comfort (blankets, sleeping bags, ponchos,

  • First-aid (assorted gauze/bandages, tape, scissors, creams/ointments, burn spray, ace bandages, splints, assorted medicines)

  • Toiletries: (TP, soap/shampoo, razors/cream, toothpaste/brushes, feminine hygiene, waste containment/disposal)

Other Items:

  • Communications (AM/FM/shortwave/weather radio, walkie-talkies, CB radio, HAM)

  • Barter Items (cash, precious metals, tobacco/liquor, candy)

  • Electrical Power (short term: batteries, generator & fuel - long term: windmill, solar chargers or portable systems)

  • Knowledge: (Electronic good, hard-copies best - military/survival manuals, guide to local edibles, medical reference, DIY stuff)
